solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Holy area in outskirts of Samarkand

indicators.note: the land measure goes inside the pair of outer letters
the outskirts of a word are its outermost letters, here the first and last of the city's name

parts.note: an acre is a unit of area

explanation.surface: A sacred place lies on the edge of the old Silk Road city of Samarkand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something holy is consecrated or revered, which is the meaning of sacred.

clue.text: He'd put in cryptic clues in the list

indicators.note: put in signals one set of letters placed inside another
cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters of clues are disguised by rearrangement

parts.note: the contraction He'd without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A setter has inserted cryptic clues into the programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' is the anagram signal and 'put in' the container signal; the surface reads as a setter slipping clues into a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a timetable or list of planned items.

clue.text: What a change it makes to one's winnings!

definitions.text: What a change it makes to one's winnings!

indicators.note: makes signals the letters of the preceding words being formed into something new

explanation.surface: An exclamation about how much a result alters one's prize money.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CHANGE IT rearrange to the answer; the whole clue also describes it, since dishonest play changes what you win.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheating at gambling or games alters how much one wins, unfairly.

clue.text: There's no advantage in breaking it

definitions.text: There's no advantage in breaking it

parts.words: There's no advantage in breaking it
parts.note: breaking a record usually counts as an achievement, but breaking this level just means finishing with neither profit nor loss

explanation.surface: Advice that smashing something brings no benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: To break even is to end up level, with no gain or loss.

indicators.note: upset tells us the letters of the preceding words are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A star figure skater is distressed after a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is upset' is the anagram signal, yet its 'is' also belongs to the fodder alongside 'skater'.
explanation.definitionFit: A typographical star symbol, the little printed mark used for footnotes, is called an asterisk.

clue.text: So unholy cads may be converted here

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged, with a religious hint

explanation.surface: Wicked rogues might be brought to faith at a church class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be converted' rearranges SO UNHOLY CADS; 'here' points to the place where such conversion could happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Children receive religious instruction at this weekly church class, the place where conversion might occur.

clue.text: Former graduate set up test paper

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are raised and so read upwards

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A one-time graduate prepared an examination paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a written test paper.

clue.text: A lady well-liked on the network

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a grid is a network of lines

explanation.surface: A popular woman on the electricity network.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a woman's name, so it is an example of a lady.

clue.text: Shrewish girl set about painter in unarmed combat

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so the girl's name encloses the painter

parts.note: Kate is the shrew in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
RA, Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered girl attacked an artist with her bare hands.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is a stock crossword painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese martial art of fighting without weapons.

indicators.note: caught means holding something, so the letters of he'd enclose the fish

parts.note: the contraction he'd written without its apostrophe
an eel is a long snakelike fish

explanation.surface: An angler tilted his rod as he landed a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' is the container signal. 'Angled' suggests fishing, but here it means leaning over, as a ship heels.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that has heeled is tilted or leaning to one side, so heeled means angled.

clue.text: Peace-making counsel is put at risk

parts.note: advice to make peace would be to finish off one's fury: end anger
advice to make peace would be to finish off one's fury: end anger

explanation.surface: Advice from a peacemaker is jeopardised.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's opening phrase is read as a two-word instruction, END plus ANGER, which run together as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger something is to expose it to harm, the same as putting it at risk.

parts.note: suggests an unmarried older woman, but means a female servant of olden times who waited at table

explanation.surface: An elderly spinster.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern or household servant girl of former times was a maid in the sense of a servant.

definitions.meaning: customs or excise ... is a levy charged on imported or sold goods
a soldier on ... is performing service

explanation.definitionFit: Duty means both a levy on imports and a task performed as service or obligation.

indicators.note: retires means draws back, so the word for elderly is read in reverse

parts.note: aged describes someone when they are old

explanation.surface: An elderly painter steps back and moves south to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retires' is the reversal signal. Edgar Degas was the French Impressionist painter of ballet dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas is a celebrated example of a French Impressionist painter.

definitions.meaning: the parliament of Japan, and historically assemblies in Europe

explanation.definitionFit: Diet means both a controlled eating regimen and a legislative assembly such as Japan's parliament.

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word is wrapped round the second

parts.note: to do is to perform

explanation.surface: People are about to carry out an act of devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are about to' looks like a single phrase meaning 'will soon'; split it into ARE and the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore is to worship or revere deeply.

definitions.meaning: to opt for or choose something
to set upon someone, as a dog might

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to choose something and to lunge at someone.

clue.text: Not a short class in arithmetic

definitions.text: Not a short class in arithmetic

parts.words: Not a short class in arithmetic
parts.note: reads as a lengthy maths lesson, but means the written method of dividing by a large number, set against its shorter sibling method

explanation.surface: A maths lesson that drags on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: Arithmetic has short and lengthy methods of dividing numbers; the clue points at the one that is not short.

clue.text: First Lieutenant in boat gives a tip

indicators.note: in signals the letter going inside the vessel's name

parts.note: a pinnace is a small boat carried on a ship

indicators.note: first picks only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A ship's first lieutenant hands over a gratuity aboard the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lieutenant' suggests a naval rank, but gives only L, put inside PINNACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is a high peak or tip, as of a mountain or building.

parts.note: a chance is an opening or opportunity
RY is short for railway, which runs on lines

explanation.surface: The case opens with lines spoken in court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Court of Chancery was a former English court of equity.

parts.note: someone from Paris is French
polish means refinement or elegance, like chic

explanation.surface: An elegant coat shows off a stylish Parisian look.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy shellac finish applied to wood furniture is a type of smooth coating known by this name.

definitions.meaning: tests, as legal hearings or experiments

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both troubles endured and formal tests or hearings.

indicators.note: topless means the first letter, the top in a down clue, is taken off

parts.note: to revolve is to go round

explanation.surface: Spin around without a shirt on, and grow.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve is to develop gradually.

indicators.note: casually suggests the letters are arranged in a careless, haphazard order

explanation.surface: Stroll over in a relaxed manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To rove is to roam or wander about without a fixed destination.

clue.text: Take the plunge, but get nothing in exchange

indicators.note: the round zero sits inside the word for a trade

parts.note: swop is a variant spelling of swap, to exchange
O looks like zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A risk-taker dives in yet gains nothing from the trade.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoop is to dive down suddenly, a literal taking of the plunge.

parts.note: non is French for no, a refusal

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's refusal is coming shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned word meaning shortly or in a little while.

definitions.meaning: metal beaten into a thin sheet, as in kitchen wrapping

explanation.definitionFit: Foil names both thin sheet metal and the light sword used in fencing.

clue.text: Playboy making love in the French way

indicators.note: in signals the zero going inside the French street

parts.note: rue is French for street, a way
love means zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A ladies' man courting in the Gallic manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A roue is a dissolute man devoted to pleasure, much like a playboy.

definitions.meaning: Humpty Dumpty, the nursery-rhyme egg, is rounded on every side

explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated word means versatile or comprehensive, and read literally means spherical on every side like an egg.

clue.text: It is said to have proved a hit

definitions.text: It is said to have proved a hit

parts.words: It is said to have proved a hit
parts.note: a fencer calls out this French word to acknowledge being struck, and it is also said on conceding a good point in argument

explanation.surface: Something spoken to admit a successful strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencers use this French exclamation to acknowledge a hit by the opponent.

indicators.note: sort is read as a verb, to arrange, so the following letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A secretive type of headwear fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy and furtive both describe acting quietly and secretively to avoid notice.

clue.text: Only just get me to bank

parts.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: Someone barely managing asks to be trusted with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Merely means simply or no more than, matching only or just.
